claims.text: A page exists in the Pulumi docs at /docs/support/provider-support-policy/ (the link target for the 'Provider support policy' card on the support index page).
Pulumi's provider support policy page describes how long Pulumi maintains each provider major version.
Pulumi's provider support policy page describes which providers get long-term security updates, implying some Pulumi providers receive long-term security updates.
Pulumi focuses on actively supporting the latest released major version of the providers it maintains.
For a set of widely used providers, Pulumi ships security updates for the previous major version for up to a year, or until the next major version is released, whichever comes first.
The Pulumi provider support policy page at /docs/support/provider-support-policy/ lists the covered providers and what a long-term support release contains.
Older major versions of Pulumi-maintained providers receive no patches at all.
The Pulumi Registry (/registry/) shows the current version for all providers maintained by Pulumi.
The page /docs/support/provider-support-policy/ exists (Provider support policy).
Pulumi does not automatically roll back changes during an update if an error occurs; it completes pending in-progress operations, then exits and reports the error.
Pulumi does not query the cloud provider's live state before running pulumi up or pulumi preview unless refresh is requested.
`pulumi up --refresh` refreshes and applies desired state in a single step.
Pulumi Cloud provides built-in drift detection for scheduled automated drift detection and remediation.
Pulumi auto-naming appends a random suffix to the logical name and enables creating replacement resources before deleting old ones.
Pulumi Cloud manages a unique encryption key per stack, configurable to use a custom secrets provider; the same value encrypts differently across stacks.
Pulumi does not use the Terraform engine; some Pulumi providers use Terraform schemas, while Pulumi native providers map directly to cloud provider APIs and do not use Terraform schemas.
Experimental Pulumi features are always opt-in, enabled via a flag, command, or environment variable such as PULUMI_EXPERIMENTAL=true, and can change or be removed without a deprecation cycle.
Each major version of a Pulumi provider includes migration logic for upgrading from the immediately previous major version.
In npm, the tilde operator (~1.2.3) allows patch updates on the current minor version.
Pulumi actively maintains the latest released major version of every provider it publishes.
For a set of widely used providers, Pulumi ships security updates for the previous major version (N-1) for up to 12 months, or until the next major version is released, whichever comes first.
The providers receiving long-term support updates are AWS, Azure Classic, Azure Native, Azure AD, Command, Docker Build, GCP, Kubernetes, TLS, and Vault.
Registry package pages exist at /registry/packages/aws/, azure, azure-native, azuread, command, docker-build, gcp, kubernetes, tls, and vault.

The LTS branch ships High/Critical CVE security patches: fixes for CVEs affecting the provider's code or direct dependencies, and fixes for broken internal infrastructure on the LTS branch needed to ship them.
An LTS release does not contain new upstream API versions, new resources or properties, performance improvements, non-security bug fixes, or compatibility with newer language runtime versions.
LTS providers remain compatible with the version of Pulumi they were frozen at unless security fixes prompt otherwise.
Exactly one long-term support major version exists per covered provider at any time.
When N+1 ships, it becomes the new N, the old N becomes the new LTS major, and the old LTS major reaches end of life the same day regardless of remaining 12-month window.
Within the LTS major, only the latest minor version receives patches; earlier minors are frozen.
LTS releases are available through the same standard package registries as current-major releases, but are tagged differently.
Customers pinning to a specific major version automatically receive patch releases as they ship, and pinning to a major version is recommended.
If v3 is the newest release, v3 is N, v2 is N−1, and v1 and earlier are end of life; older majors receive no patches.
The current major (N) receives new features, new resources, bug fixes, security patches, dependency upgrades, and new upstream API versions until N+1 ships.
End-of-life versions (N−2 and older) are not supported and receive no updates.
